newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street seen mixed at open, bias higher.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street seen mixed at open, bias higher.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were expected to open mixed to slightly higher on Monday, as the long bond firmed and following the release of April personal income which was viewed as within the range of forecasts.

The benchmark 30-year bond was up 6/89 at a 6.89 percent yield, after closing at 6.91 percent on Friday. Analysts had been worried a seven percent bond yield would prompt money managers to move funds from stocks into cash and bonds.
Bonds held their ground after the release of April personal income and consumption data, which were each up 0.1 percent. Both were expected to be unchanged.
"The data was essentially in-line," Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments, said.
"The bond market is higher after the release of the data and because of a firmer dollar, and stocks should get help if bonds continue to strengthen," he said.
The Standard & Poor's 500 futures index was up 2.15 points at 852.75.

The dollar started the week higher against after the mark after a victory by the left in the French general elections increased uncertainty about Europe's plans for a single currency. It was trading at 1.7264/74 marks.
